title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) measuring whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents using gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline emulator executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract this degenerate confirmatory outcome is the algebraic consequence when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We report the preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-on confirmatory designs able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level network configurations. This intent→configuration automation can speed change pipelines but risks silently violating reachability, access-control, ordering, or workflow invariants and thereby causing outages if generated text is executed without additional checks. A standard operational mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that combines stochastic LLM generation with deterministic verification and, if needed, repair or human review. Despite architectural proposals and prototypes, systematic preregistered experiments that measure a verifier's detection performance against executed outcomes under tightly controlled paired designs are scarce.

This paper answers a narrowly scoped, preregistered research question: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? That estimand isolates verifier detection from improvements that could arise from re-sampling, prompt-engineering, or repair-enabled iterations. We executed study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 across 72 preregistered paired intents under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The run completed with no technical failures and produced a degenerate confirmatory outcome (no baseline emulator faults). Rather than dismissing this as a null failure, we analyze why it occurred given the preregistered contract and archived artifacts, and we provide concrete, artifact-grounded guidance for designs that can detect verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.
sections.related_work: Prior work shows LLMs can translate high-level intent into device-level configurations in constrained vendor-dialect settings and curated evaluations [1]. Multi-agent and tool‑augmented frameworks illustrate practical architectures for integrating verifiers and domain tools into NetOps workflows and prototype deployments, but public evaluations typically rely on emulators or curated scenarios rather than preregistered paired detector measurements [2]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are well studied in code and software-repair domains where deterministic checks plus repair/resampling can materially improve correctness—importantly, the empirical utility of verification depends on baseline generator error rates and whether repairs or resampling are permitted by the workflow [3]. Canonical deterministic network-verification techniques (e.g., header-space style reachability/policy analyzers) provide semantics-aware invariants suited to the verify stage, but the supplied literature lacks preregistered paired experiments that couple LLM generation with such verifiers and measure detection against executed emulator outcomes [4]. Our study directly targets that gap by adopting a shared_initial_candidate paired design and reporting exact execution accounting to make the detection question reproducible and auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis (H1) targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 (two-sided α=0.05, power ≥0.80); a heuristic required ≈63 pairs and we preregistered N=72 pairs stratified equally across three topology-difficulty strata. The full preregistration, frozen analysis plan, exclusion rules, and sensitivity analyses are archived under the study identifier.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. The execution_contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent we performed exactly one initial LLM generation and evaluated that identical candidate in two paired conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record whether an emulator-observed operational fault occurs. Guarded: run the canonical deterministic verifier on the identical candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no executed fault); if not flagged, execute the identical candidate in the emulator and record the result. By construction, any observed paired difference can only arise from the verifier preventing execution of a candidate that would otherwise have failed at emulation; this isolates detector utility from generator-side resampling or repair effects.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration (artifact-grounded). The declared model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json) requested via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Key recorded model parameters include declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1. The recorded temperature = null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics were used (i.e., temperature was not explicitly fixed to a numeric value in the archived configuration). The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 configured to run the full_intent_constraint_validation rule set. The verifier emits structured validator_traces per episode (fields: parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after final_state snapshots, violation_codes, violation_count, difficulty metadata). These per-episode traces formed the mechanistic basis for guarded decisions.

Task-bank construction, contamination controls, and stratification. Confirmatory tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task manifest encodes a natural-language intent, a machine-structured required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, preserve_unspecified_state policies, and difficulty.level tags (medium/hard/very_hard). Exact-match provenance checks against public corpus fingerprints were preregistered; no confirmatory pair was excluded for exact-match contamination. The confirmatory sample used 24 pairs per difficulty stratum as preregistered.

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retries for transient hosted-API generation errors; all provider events were logged. The run began at 2026-08-31T06:56:23.065707Z and completed at 2026-08-31T07:06:28.665518Z. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72 (one shared generation per pair). Provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 72}, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate contract.

Scoring rule and per-episode traces. For each episode the verifier produced a binary validity verdict and validator_trace JSON documenting parsing and required counts, normalized_configuration, validation snapshots, and violation codes. The scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation enforces required_sequence order, allowed_touched_fields, and preserve_unspecified_state. In the recorded run no verifier flags occurred for confirmatory pairs (violation_count = 0 across representative episodes) and no automated repair was applied (repair_applied = false).

Inference and sensitivity procedures. The primary analysis used the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor to build the 2×2 contingency table (guarded × baseline) where an undetected executed fault = 1. The pre-specified inferential test is an exact McNemar two-sided test when discordant pairs exist. We also computed paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CIs for the paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Pre-registered subgroup comparisons (topology complexity and policy type) use Holm correction; pre-registered sensitivity analyses (treat excluded pairs as failures; quantify verifier false positives) were executed by the deterministic analysis pipeline and archived. Because the run produced no exclusions and no discordant pairs these analyses reproduce the degenerate numerical conclusion.

Design tradeoffs. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates verifier detection from generator-side effects but prevents measurement of verifier-mediated resampling or repair utility; this is a deliberate construct choice that clarifies causal interpretation while narrowing the possible detectable effects. The preregistered alternatives (independent-generation arms, repair-enabled flows, adversarial seeding) are discussed below and are implementable using the same evidence-recording conventions.

sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation and boundary conditions. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics validly measures verifier detection on identical candidates; because the identical generated candidates produced zero emulator faults the verified paired outcome is a ceiling/null result: the verifier could not reduce executed faults that did not occur. The numeric outputs (n_11 = 72; paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]) follow directly from the preregistered contract and observed data. Reporting this degenerate outcome is important: it documents a reproducible case where the preregistered estimand and data-generating conditions leave no room for the verifier to demonstrate utility.

Artifact-grounded diagnostic factors. Archived artifacts permit concrete attribution of this ceiling outcome to measurable pipeline factors. First, the deterministic task generator encoded explicit required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields that constrain acceptable configs and increase the probability of a single correct generation. Second, the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that consistently matched those structured constraints across the synthetic corpus (per-episode shared_initial_candidate traces). Third, the verifier's rule set (full_intent_constraint_validation) enforces the same task-manifest constraints; per-episode validator_traces show parsed_command_count = required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for representative tasks. Together these aligned design choices—constrained intents, congruent verifier rules, and a model that produced matching sequences—explain the absence of baseline emulator faults.

Statistical and design implications. A paired confirmatory test targeting a fixed absolute reduction requires a non-zero baseline prevalence of executed faults to have power; when baseline prevalence is zero the paired difference must be zero regardless of verifier performance. This is an algebraic consequence of the estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics, not a paradoxical failure. Confirmatory designs intended to measure verifier detection should ensure the task bank yields a measurable baseline error rate (e.g., include ambiguous intents, adversarial cases, or known failure-mode seeds) or should permit condition-specific sampling or repair so that the verifier can alter the executed-candidate distribution.

Concrete preregisterable alternatives to detect verifier utility. The archived pipeline supports several clear preregisterable modifications that enable non-degenerate inference without inventing new artifacts: (1) independent-generation arms: allow separate initial generator calls per condition (baseline vs guarded) so the verifier or guarded workflow can influence candidate distributions via resampling or repair; (2) repair-enabled flows: permit verifier-triggered deterministic repair (one repair attempt) and then execute the repaired candidate to measure end-to-end improvement; (3) adversarial/fault-injection task banks: seed tasks with ordering subtleties or vendor-edge cases to raise baseline error prevalence; (4) sampling-parameter sweeps and multi-model comparisons: explicitly set non-null temperature and test multiple model versions to quantify sampling- and model-sensitivity; (5) false-positive cost arms: measure operational blocking cost by comparing outcomes when verifier blocks flagged candidates versus when blocked candidates are repaired and re-executed. These alternatives are preregisterable under the same evidence conventions and are implementable using the archived scripts. The preregistration identifier c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 documents the sensitivity scripts and alternative-contract templates available in the archive.

Threats to validity and operational implications. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates verifier detection but prevents verifier-mediated resampling or repair effects; deterministic provider-call audit confirms one shared generation per pair. Construct validity: emulator-executed faults are a conservative surrogate for operational harm but do not capture traffic-dependent timing or hardware idiosyncrasies. External validity: the run used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic task bank; extrapolation to other models or production deployments is limited. Conclusion validity: with zero baseline faults the preregistered power analysis built to detect a 0.20 absolute reduction is moot; future confirmatory designs should align expected baseline prevalence with power targets.

Measured tradeoffs. The observed ceiling does not imply verifiers are unnecessary: under constrained, high-clarity intents and a verifier rule set that encodes the same constraints, an LLM can produce sequences that pass deterministic checks and emulator execution. In production settings with incomplete intents, noisy telemetry, or dialect variation, verifiers remain a principled guard. Measuring verifier net operational value requires preregistered trade-off quantification: estimate true-positive detection rates on task banks with non-negligible baseline faults and quantify false-positive blocking costs. The archived artifacts and deterministic accounting here provide a reproducible template for those targeted, powered follow-up experiments.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under the shared_initial_candidate contract. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires preregistered contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived responses, task manifests, validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs provide a reproducible baseline and a template for powered follow-on confirmatory designs.

Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and orchestration: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in the archived model configuration) orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: the baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per-condition generation, multi-sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single-model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling-parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private training-data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
